annotationRationale: The decisive step is computing a proportion within the group reporting dislikes. Percentage multiplication gives the sizes of its two parts.
sourceMethod: Follows the official calculation of the two groups as percentages of the school, then divides the desired part by their combined size.

review.mathCheck: Of all students, 12% like dancing but report disliking it, while 36% dislike it and report that truthfully. Therefore 12/(12+36)=1/4=25%, choice D. The denominator includes every reported disliker.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of official solution 11 on page 4: compute the two reported-dislike groups and divide the desired group by their total. The explanation makes the conditioning explicit without requiring advanced notation.
review.annotationCheck: Conditional probability is assessed through the restricted denominator; percentage multiplication is supporting knowledge. No missing case or unjustified step.
